condition: How much wheat is imported through Hudaydah
note: Split from YG-502 (review, returns-2): one food through one port, beside all food imports through each side's ports.

condition: Where electronic payment means reach
note: Split from YG-509 (review, returns-2): where they reach holds together with how widely they are available.

condition: Whether formal financial services are accessible
note: Split from YG-513 (review, returns-2): whether services are accessible holds together with the share that holds an account, which these rows give without a figure.

condition: How wholesalers prefer to be paid
note: Split from YG-521 (review, returns-2, rule 1): what wholesalers prefer holds together with how businesses pay their suppliers.

condition: Whether Yemenia honours tickets its Sana'a office issued
note: Split from YG-525 (review, returns-2, rule 1): honouring tickets issued in Sana'a holds together with issuing tickets in Houthi-controlled areas.

condition: Where internet service reaches
what_varies: coverage gaps, sparse or widely available
note: Split from YG-552 (review, returns-2): coverage holds together with how reliable service is. YQ-E706 and E707 came from YG-551 (review, returns-2); they come from one source on one date and disagree.

condition: What share of people have mobile internet
note: Split from YG-551 (review, returns-2): access to 3G or mobile internet is a different measure from internet access.

condition: What internet data costs as a share of income
what_varies: the share of monthly income per head
note: Split from YG-555 (review, returns-2): a cost as a share of income holds together with how costly access is.

condition: Who controls internet and telecom services
what_varies: Ansar Allah through YemenNet, or each party's monopoly in its area
note: Split from YG-556 (review, returns-2, rule 1): who controls the sector holds together with which providers operate.

condition: How many internet and telecom providers may operate
note: Split from YG-556 (review, returns-2), as above.

condition: How many mobile subscriptions there are per 100 people
note: Split from YG-560 (review, returns-2): subscriptions are a different measure from the share of people who use a mobile phone.

condition: How many people have access to electricity
note: Split from YG-561 (review, returns-2): access holds together with how reliable supply is. Second review: those cut off from grid-supplied electricity (YQ-E239) are YG-739.

condition: Whether a central bank's new coins and notes circulate or are accepted in practice
what_varies: circulating in everyday trade, or refused, for the coin or note named
note: Split from YG-026 (second review, YA-17, rule 1): what circulates or is accepted in practice holds together with the rules on whether the coins and notes may be used, as YG-568 is split from YG-024 for prints.

condition: Whether money transfers in Houthi-controlled areas are tied to one specified network, with ceilings
what_varies: tied to one specified network, with strict ceilings
note: Split from YG-106 (second review, YA-51, the brief's parts of one source): item 006 states this beside the ban on the unified network (YQ-D029), and the two hold together.

condition: Which banks are linked to the national switch for money transfers
note: Split from YG-107 (second review, YA-52, rule 1): item 059 reports the national switch ('نظام المقسم الوطني') apart from the unified network ('الشبكة الموحدة', YQ-C389).

condition: Cost of sending money to Yemen by channel (banks, Western Union, informal offices)
note: Split from YG-623 (second review, YA-220): costs by channel, by provider and surveyed fees are different measures that hold together.

condition: What fees migrants surveyed paid to send money to Yemen
what_varies: the fees most respondents paid per transfer
note: Split from YG-623 (second review, YA-220), as above.

condition: Whether a phone wallet's cash is available around the clock
note: Split from YG-638 (second review, YA-225, the brief's parts of one source): the Cash wallet's listing gives cash around the clock, which its English page explains as cash-out through ATMs outside working hours (YE-E774, YQ-E685); this holds together with withdrawals at agents during official working hours (YQ-C127).

condition: Whether the number of phone wallets may exceed 15, by an interviewee's estimate
note: Split from YG-640 (second review, YA-226): item 077 gives the possible total beside its count of 8 to 10 (YQ-C461) and sets neither against the other, so the two hold together.

condition: Whether customs revenue can be paid in e-rials through CAC Bank
what_varies: CAC Bank permitted to collect it
note: Split from YG-432 (second review, YA-165): one permission for one payment holds together with the general state of public revenue payments, as the review round split registration fees, taxes and a business wallet's payments.

condition: What share of the whole population holds a bank account
note: Split from YG-513 (second review, YA-197): the share of the whole population and the share of adults are two measures that hold at one time.

condition: Whether telecom and internet services still function despite damage to the sector
note: Split from YG-552 (second review, YA-206): services that still function at a basic level hold together with frequent outages; the source adds that the sector is becoming increasingly fragile.

condition: How many people are cut off from grid-supplied electricity
note: Split from YG-728 (second review, YA-241): those cut off from the grid and those with access to electricity are two measures that hold at one time.

condition: How many exchange businesses a central bank has licensed or registered
what_varies: the count of licensed or registered companies, establishments, outlets and agents, by central bank
note: Split from YG-131 (independent review, finding 7): the count of licensed or registered businesses and the count of all money exchangers can hold at once, and item 073 gives both (YE-D475, YE-D478), so each measure is its own condition. Joins parts D: items 073 (registered with each central bank) and 076 (licensed).

condition: Which payment options a guide lists for use in Yemen
note: Split from YG-125 (independent review, finding 5): Wise's guide lists Wise among the best payment options for use in Yemen, which states no availability; the guide's other options are in the conditions they answer (YQ-E575 to E578).

condition: Whether an account in Yemen can receive money through an international payment service
what_varies: can or cannot receive, at the service named
note: Split from YG-125 (independent review, check of S-01's axes, item 1): YQ-D634's source gives receiving apart from sending (YE-D997), and no other row gives receiving alone. YG-125's rows give payments from or to Yemen together, so they stay there.

condition: What a payment service provider licence requires
what_varies: the legal form and minimum capital
note: Joins parts D and F; both rest on the Aden central bank's instructions of September 2022. The news report (YQ-D119) gives 700 million for a system operator where the instrument (YQ-F080) gives 750; the instrument's words govern, and the report's figure is in YQ-D119's note (check of the S-01 entry's axes, must fix 2).
